comparison: Perfect agreement on α7-nAChR receptor identification (C37-C48). Both evaluations find the evidence solid, with peer reviewers highlighting the novelty of the α7-nAChR mechanism and praising the human scRNA-seq validation for clinical relevance.

Perfect agreement on Wnt-independence claims (C100-C102). Both evaluations accept the interpretation that nicotine's effects are independent of Wnt activation, supported by CHIR99021 experiments and Apc-mutant model data. Peer reviewer explicitly confirms this discussion was included.

Strong agreement on organoid formation and Paneth cell independence (C30-C36). OpenEval emphasizes dose-dependent effects and co-culture experiments; peer reviewers highlight this as a 'noteworthy research highlight' and 'novel insight' showing direct ISC effects independent of Paneth cells. Peer result also includes C86 from the integrated model.

Strong agreement on DBZ tumor prevention (C8, C83-C84). Both find evidence supportive, though OpenEval notes C84 slightly overstates findings as only prevention was tested. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the Notch signaling mechanism without specific concerns. Peer result also includes C87 from the integrated model.

Strong agreement on PKC signaling role (C49-C53). OpenEval finds evidence supportive; peer reviewer initially had concerns about PKC inhibitor effects but explicitly states these were resolved with additional Sotrastaurin data, now accepting the finding.

Strong agreement on nicotine-induced tumorigenesis in Apc-mutant mice (C7, C79-C82). Both evaluations find the tumor formation data compelling, with peer reviewers praising the use of stem cell-specific Apc knockout model as a strength.

Strong agreement on YAP/TAZ and Notch activation in ISCs (C59-C65). OpenEval emphasizes cell-type specificity demonstrated by sorted cell analysis; peer reviewers confirm the signaling cascade as a 'key driver' and note sufficient experimental evidence provided.

Strong agreement on in vivo ISC expansion findings (C3, C25-C29). Both find immunostaining data solid and well-supported. OpenEval covers broader claim set including C22-C24 and C27; peer reviewers emphasize use of Lgr5 reporter mice as a strength. Peer result R9 also addresses histological details C22-C24.

Strong agreement on YAP/Notch epistasis and feedback loop (C69-C70, C73-C76). OpenEval emphasizes DBZ experiments demonstrating positive feedback; peer reviewers accept Notch as essential in the signaling process. OpenEval also covers C71-C72 (cited literature) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers.

Agreement on YAP/Notch requirement downstream of α7-nAChR/PKC (C66-C68). OpenEval emphasizes epistasis experiments with pathway inhibitors; peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall signaling mechanism without specific concerns.

Agreement on histological details of ISC expansion (C22-C24). OpenEval includes these as part of broader in vivo findings (R1); peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss these details but affirm overall findings as solid.

Agreement on exclusion of alternative pathways (C54-C55). OpenEval explicitly supports exclusion of PI3K/AKT, p38/MAPK, mTORC1; peer reviewer implicitly accepts this as part of 'systematic investigation' of pathways, though not explicitly discussed.

Both address integrated model claims. OpenEval R10 covers comprehensive model (C85-C87, C112) including Paneth cell independence; peer R2 specifically highlights Paneth cell independence (C86) as a noteworthy finding.
Both address integrated model claims. OpenEval R10 includes C87 (overall signaling pathway model); peer R8 addresses therapeutic implications (C87) as part of DBZ tumor prevention findings.

Both address human translational relevance (C43). OpenEval R15 specifically evaluates human scRNA-seq data showing CHRNA7 expression; peer R3 explicitly praises this analysis as strengthening clinical relevance.
OpenEval identifies C99 as unsupported due to 'data not shown' statement. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not flag this as a concern.
OpenEval evaluates background/cited literature claims (C1-C2, C9-C21) as appropriately supported by citations. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background claims.
OpenEval evaluates extensive cited prior work (C56-C58, C71-C72, C88-C95, C97-C98, C103-C108, C117-C121) as appropriately cited. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these background citations.
